title: Minimum Wage Victoria: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay
description: Understand the minimum wage in Victoria and how to convert hourly pay to annual salary using the 38-hour week, tax, super, and casual loading. Free guide.
salarySummary: Based on a 38-hour week, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour gives an annual gross of about $52,300, with super paid on top.

faqs.q: What is the minimum wage in Victoria for 2026–27?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage applies in Victoria. From 1 July 2026 it is $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week, or $1,004.90 per week. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour. Award rates may be higher.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52. If you work a standard 38-hour week, use 38. For example, $30 per hour × 38 × 52 = $59,280 gross per year. This assumes no unpaid overtime or penalty rates.

faqs.q: Does superannuation come out of my hourly rate?
faqs.a: No. Super guarantee is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026 the rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. It is not deducted from your hourly pay.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Minimum Wage Victoria and Annual Pay Conversion

If you are paid by the hour or have a salary offer, converting between hourly and annual figures helps you compare jobs and budget. This guide explains the process using the standard 38-hour week, the National Minimum Wage, tax, and superannuation. We focus on **minimum wage victoria** because state averages differ from national figures.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly × Hours × 52

Annual gross pay is your hourly rate multiplied by the hours you work each week, multiplied by 52 weeks. For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, the formula is:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour. That gives:

$26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,269.44 per year (rounded to $52,270).

If you are a casual worker, you receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate. The casual minimum is $33.05 per hour. Using the same formula:

$33.05 × 38 × 52 = $65,306.80 per year.

This calculation assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. It is a starting point for comparing offers.

### Why 38 Hours? The Standard Work Week

Under the Fair Work Act, the standard full-time week is 38 hours. Many awards and agreements use this as the base. When you see a salary quoted as "per year" without hours, it usually assumes 38 hours. If you work more or fewer hours, adjust the formula accordingly. For part-time or casual roles, use your actual weekly hours.

### Fortnightly Pay: A Handy Check

If you are paid fortnightly, multiply your weekly gross by 2. For the minimum wage of $26.44 per hour:

Weekly: $26.44 × 38 = $1,004.72 (close to the Fair Work figure of $1,004.90).
Fortnightly: $1,004.72 × 2 = $2,009.44.

This helps you verify your pay slip. Remember that tax and super are calculated on your ordinary earnings, not on the gross amount after loading.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates vs Victoria Averages

The National Minimum Wage is the legal floor. Many industries have award rates that are higher. For example, the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page on this site lists current rates. In Victoria, full-time ordinary time earnings averaged $2,041.10 per week in May 2026, according to the Australian Bureau of Statistics. That is an average for all full-time employees in Victoria, not a median for any specific job. Your actual rate may be above or below that average.

Casual employees receive a 25% loading as compensation for not receiving paid leave. The loading is applied to the base hourly rate. When using our [timesheet](/), you can check the box to add 25% casual loading on top of your base rate. Do not enter a rate that already includes loading.

### Tax on Your Annual Pay

Once you have your annual gross, you can estimate tax using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% of excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30% of excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37% of excess over $135,000
- $190,001+: $51,370 plus 45% of excess over $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (based on 2025–26 single reduction thresholds, as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed). For a minimum wage earner on $52,270:

Tax: $4,020 + 30% × ($52,270 – $45,000) = $4,020 + $2,181 = $6,201.
Medicare: 2% × $52,270 = $1,045.40.
Total tax and Medicare: about $7,246.

Take-home pay: $52,270 – $7,246 = $45,024 per year, or about $866 per week.

For a more detailed breakdown, see our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, paid by your employer on top of your gross pay. It does not reduce your take-home pay. The maximum earnings that attract super is $270,830 per year (the maximum contribution base). For a minimum wage earner, super is:

12% × $52,270 = $6,272.40 per year.

This goes into your super fund, not your pocket. If you salary sacrifice or have a higher income, the rules change. See our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page for more.

### Using the Hourly to Annual Conversion

Our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool lets you enter your base hourly rate and see annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures. Remember:

- The annual figure is hourly × hours per week × 52.
- We assume 38 hours unless you enter a different number.
- Casual loading is added via a checkbox; do not include it in your base rate.
- Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top.
- Tax uses the 2026–27 scale with the full tax-free threshold.

This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax. For exact figures, consult your pay slip, the [pay guides](/blog) for your award, or speak to a tax professional.

### State Differences: Victoria vs National

While the National Minimum Wage applies across Australia, average earnings vary by state. In Victoria, full-time ordinary time earnings were $2,041.10 per week in May 2026, compared to the national average of $2,083.70. That is about 2% lower. However, these are averages, not medians for any particular job. Your industry or role may pay more or less. For job-specific pay data, refer to [job pay](/topics/job-pay) resources.

### Summary

Converting your hourly rate to annual pay is straightforward: multiply by hours per week and 52. For minimum wage victoria, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour gives about $52,270 per year before tax and super. Casual workers get $33.05 per hour, or about $65,307 per year. Always check your award or agreement for the correct rate. Use our [reference tables](/data) for current figures.
